contract_issues: ma_commit qualification: SOC.md 3.8 / v1_core pulse ma_commit for every acked arch access, but URC must count only UTLB-translated, non-faulting accesses that are not a PREF outside the SQ (mmu 3.6), and v1_mmu cannot pair an MA ack with its EX translation. Exact fix: add a 'cnt' bit to dxlat_t driven by v1_mmu and set ma_commit = lreq.v & lrsp.ack & lreq.arch & lreq.x.cnt. Interim fix (no package change): v1_soc passes core.ma_commit & v1_mmu_pkg::mmu_urc_counts(lreq, mmu.at, ccr.ora) to v1_mmu; it is tested at unit level and in the bm run. Without either fix the SoC's D1/R4 URC records fail.

SOC.md 3.8's xl_stall rule ('1 while the EX access uses the UTLB CAM') deadlocks: the access behind an OC associative array write is held in EX for every cycle of that write. v1_utlb gives EX its own compare port D; xl_stall is 1 only in the ITLB refill's one UTLB search cycle. SOC.md should say that.

dxlat_t.c now includes CCR.OCE (answers WI-P4's VOLRD contract note; mmu 3.4 'cacheable when C=1 and CCR.OCE=1'; SOC.md is silent). SOC.md should state it for WI-CACHE. if_c still excludes CCR.ICE per SOC.md 3.2.1.
Commit records from v1_mmu carry isn=0 because v1_mmu has no ISN input. WI-SOC must stamp LDTLB with the LDTLB micro-op's ISN and ITLBFILL with tap.core.next_isn.
open_questions: mmu Q4 (CAM port sharing between the refill search and data accesses), Q9 (whether IC/OC associative writes with AT=1 update LRUI/URC) and Q11 (user mode with SV=1 compares the ASID) could each be settled by one safe KOS probe. I ran none: acceptance does not need them, and the RTL follows the manual or the spec's proposal.
261 of the bm port's 1301 records (timing / fetch / ic / pmc / pipeline / oc) can only be checked on the full SoC at M2 by WI-SOC with tb/bm/mmu/expect.py check.
WI-REF's sh4_sys.h uses its own stand-in sh4sys::MmuRef; switching it to mmuref::Sh4Mmu needs a thin MmuIf adapter (WI-REF's decision).
impl:WI-MMU.notes:
I resumed after the crash. The killed agent's RTL, testbench, model and bm port were complete and correct on review, but it had written no report. My changes:
(1) CCR.OCE is folded into dxl.c.
(2) New v1_mmu_pkg::mmu_urc_counts for the ma_commit qualification, exposed as urc_cnt in the tb and checked on every data comparison.
(3) The random test distribution is repaired. TI had fired about 15 times per batch, and random ASIDs and 1 MB LDTLB pages left only 1.9% of vectors as translated hits. Now 16% are clean translations and every outcome class has at least 46k vectors.
(4) New self-tests: model mutations 11/12, RTL plants oce/urcfx/urcpref, extra D1 rows, and the bm runners now take CCR from the program; run_rtl drives ma_commit from the RTL's own qualification.
Everything was rebuilt from clean. Scratch logs are in agents/scratch/WI-MMU/. No files outside WI-MMU's were edited, no git commits, no hardware used.

contract_issues: ubc_ctl_t has no SEQ bit. With BRCR.SEQ=1 a channel-A tag must reach its break point (hit_a, event 0x19) without breaking, and the core cannot know that. v1_ubc exports an extra output ctl_seq; core rule: break when (A && !ctl_seq) || (B && ctl.b_live). Suggest adding 'seq' to ubc_ctl_t.

SOC.md 1.3.2 / 4.1 item 7 give v1_fetch an input ubc_pre_armed, but nothing drives it, and only v1_ubc knows BBRx. v1_ubc exports an extra output ctl_pre_armed (fetch-side copy: ID[0] & RW[0] & !PCBx on either channel; 0 while the UBC is idle). Suggest adding 'pre_armed' to ubc_ctl_t and naming the source in 4.1 item 7.

Spec debug-ubc-hudi 4.1 says MOVCA.L has no data. Manual 20.3.1 / 20.3.5(3), which the spec cites, lists only PREF, OCBP, OCBWB and OCBI as accesses without data. The model follows the manual: MOVCA.L is a size-L write carrying R0. The ubc_opq_t.nodata comment ('PREF / cache op') should exclude MOVCA.L. The per-kind opq mapping for WI-CORE-A is in v1_ubc.sv's header: PREF/OCBP/OCBWB read L nodata; OCBI write L nodata; MOVCA.L write L with data; TAS.B read+write byte, the purge presents nothing; FMOV quad one size-Q access.

SOC.md 1.3.1 says the operand-break tag is 'set in EX'. The console's operand-settle boundary (k=2 no break, k=3 break) requires the core to take the combinational opm in the cycle the access micro-op LEAVES EX, because the load waits in EX under the P4 write's mah until the write's MA3.

SOC.md 2.5 says cpu_run holds every flop of v1_perfctr and of the UBC's core side. I gate the counting, the event registers, 'A seen', the CMF sets and the events. Register writes from the bridge are not gated [P]; otherwise a DMAC on-chip write while the CPU sleeps would be acked and lost.
open_questions: Fetch run-ahead depth (WI-CORE-B; spec 10.2). The UBC settle vectors fit a 5- or 6-halfword run-ahead, and SOC.md 4.1 item 5 keeps v1's 4. The UBC side (IF_DLY=3) is final either way. With v1's 4, ubcevt S ADD k=9/10 break one fetch early in the M1b replay; with IF_DLY=4 NOP 13/14 would miss instead.
Event 0x22 per OC fill: about 14 per write-miss fill in pmcsurvey stmiss against 24 per read-miss fill in spec 7.3 ocm (WI-CACHE's C18 calibration).

Unchanged spec items, kept [P]: reserved BAM/SZ encodings, follower-lane data breaks, TRAPA priority (10.3); PMCLK at other FRQCR (10.5); PMC power-on values (10.6); the stale-bus source of the UBC_NODRV window (10.8).
impl:WI-DBG.notes:
Resumed after the crash. The previous agent had finished nearly all of WI-DBG: the four units, the testbenches, sh4_dbg.h, the bm ports, and the 9.6 survey (run once on hardware, clean). I verified every file against SOC.md and the spec and re-ran all checks.
Fixes and additions this session:
- ctl_pre_armed: the missing driver of v1_fetch.ubc_pre_armed.
- The C++ model's oper(): the ISS's size-0 cache ops were treated as quadword; now PREF/OCB*/MOVCA are longword, TAS purge is skipped, and MOVCA.L carries data per the manual.
- A 'kinds' tb section, a lint target with a package-only waiver, 15 more mutants (34/34 caught), a check.py self-test (558/558), and run-ahead 6 in the settle report.
- No hardware run this session: 9.6 was already settled, and 9.5 needs no hardware for the UBC side.
Timing mechanisms and the numbers they produce:
- PMC: MA1 read, end-of-MA3 write and two event registers give 0 3 6 9 / 21 and the A.3 table.
- UBC: a 3-stage write-forward pipeline to the fetch-side copy gives the NOP k=13 settle point; the EX compare on the live registers gives the operand k=3 point.
Other: make v1 was not run, as the WI does not require it. All outputs are under agents/verify/WI-DBG and agents/scratch/WI-DBG; mutant build logs are in build/v1_dbg_mut (gitignored). Nothing was committed. v1_core.sv and v1_pkg.sv show as modified in git status; those changes are other WIs', not mine.

verify:WI-EXC.report:
WI-EXC is sound. Both units match the SOC.md §3.8 port lists exactly. Registers, masks, reset values, size rules, resolver order, the IRL / NMI / on-chip decision times (14/15, 8/9, 4/5) and the IMASK structure (s+9 even / s+10 odd) are all correct.

**Reproduced:**
- `make v1-intc`: 332,679 checks, 0 failures; lint clean.
- Implementer mutants: 18/18 caught.
- Bare-metal ports build; `check.py --self` passes; snippet layout matches the console ELFs mod 1 KB (0 of 663 symbols differ).

**New adversarial tests** (`agents/verify/WI-EXC`):
- 7 coverage checks pass: IRL all pins × IRLM × IMASK, reset kinds, NMI matrix, IMASK all pairs × phase, 20k random excregs operations, standby IRL on rtc_tick, size rule and holes. A mutation run catches 8/8 planted bugs, so they can fail.
- 8 checks fail; they are the findings below.

**Findings, most severe first:**
1. **Weak M1a gate.** `v1_p4bus` + `v1_intc` put the IPRA store → irq.req at MA1+9..12, i.e. excint C1 k = 8-11, against the console's 13/17/15. `expected.json` accepts 8-21 (PI 8-24), so M1a cannot catch a 4-7 cycle calibration gap.
2. **Bug.** With MAI = 1 in standby, an NMI edge is still latched. It ends standby once the pin is high again and later appears as a spurious NMI; hm 19.4.3 says this cannot happen.
3. **Not reproducible.** The v1-schedule tables behind the §9.4 fit came from a harness lost in the crash.
4. **Package wording.** `irq.code` changes while req stays 1; the package comment says "stable while req".
5. **Unmarked [P].** Raising IMASK takes 9-10 cycles, the same as lowering. A level-10 request can be accepted with IMASK 15 up to s+8/9, which conflicts with WI-REF's legality check.
6. **excregs collision.** A DMAC bus write in the same cycle as `excw` is dropped, even for a different register.
7. **Weak gate.** Only 1 of 60 M1a exception records checks that INTEVT is kept across general exceptions.
8. **Unmarked [P].** With IRLM = 1, one shared noise canceller couples the four independent requests.
9. **Unmarked [P].** NMIB written in the `nmi_ack` cycle.
10. **Cross-unit (WI-CLK).** `v1_cpg`'s RESYNC assumes `wake` changes right after a pce; it becomes visible in ph 1 or ph 3 cycles.

The report is at `agents/reports/units/WI-EXC-verify.md`.

findings.where: tb/bm/exceptions-intc/expected.json ('C1 ipr_write', 'C1 unie_write', 'S PI ipra'); rtl/v1/v1_intc.sv IPR path (strobe -> req 6 [P]) with rtl/v1/v1_p4bus.sv posted-write strobe
findings.problem: End to end, the IPRA store -> irq.req path is 4-7 Icyc faster than the console. The expected.json regexes accept k = 8-21 (PI 8-24), so the M1a gate cannot detect it. The console value (13 / 17 / 15 x6, warm 15) is steady and warm, so no cache argument applies. TCR.UNIE gives the same console k, so the missing cycles are common to both paths (bridge strobe point or core schedule), not the INTC alone.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-EXC/run.sh (the p4intc E1 line): MA1 = x at every phase -> INTC strobe at x+3..x+6 -> irq.req at x+9..x+12 -> predicted C1 k = 8..11 (v1 schedule of t_chain_st16: add_i at x+1+i), against the console's 13..17.
findings.fix: Pin the C1 ipr_write and unie_write regexes to the console set {13, 15, 17}, with at most the documented phase spread. Record the IPR / UNIE write -> request time as a joint WI-P4 / WI-EXC M1a calibration item (SOC 9.4 / 9.13), most likely the posted-write strobe point within the 2-Pcyc drain.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_intc.sv:133-150 (nmi_edge / nmi_evt ignore MAI in standby), :298 (wake_stby); tb/sh4_intc.h set_nmi_pin / wake_stby
findings.problem: hm 19.4.3 (hm.txt 27231-27236): in standby with MAI = 1, 'an NMI interrupt is not generated by a transition at the NMI pin ... standby cannot be cleared by an NMI'. The RTL still latches the edge. It masks wake_stby only while the pin is low, so standby ends as soon as the pin goes high again. If standby ends by another source instead, the latched NMI is later taken as a spurious NMI. nmi_evt also pulses (DMAOR.NMIF).
findings.repro: agents/scratch/WI-EXC/obj_adv/adv --only A. A1: MAI = 1, standby, pin 1->0->1 gives wake_stby 0 while low, then 1 after it rises (both NMIE = 0 and NMIE = 1). A3: the same edge, then an ATI exit: the INTC presents nmi = 1, code 0x1C0 instead of 0x480, and nmi_evt pulsed once.
findings.fix: In standby with icr_mai = 1, suppress nmi_edge / nmi_evt so nothing is latched. The same change goes in Sh4Intc::set_nmi_pin and wake_stby.

findings.where: tb/v1_intc_tb.cpp:440-567 (progs boundary tables for ci2 / excint C1 / excint3 / PH)
findings.problem: These offsets are the evidence for the SOC 9.4 'one structure' fit. They came from a v1_core trace harness kept only in the session scratchpad, which the crash lost. The tb itself says the tables must be re-derived whenever WI-CORE-A changes the LDC SR / RTE / refetch schedule, and v1_core.sv is being edited now. No tool can re-derive them.
findings.repro: ls agents/scratch/ and search the repo for a trace driver of t_chain_* / t_ph* on v1_core: there is none. resume_done.json WI-EXC notes: 'a scratch harness in the session scratchpad (not in the repo)'.
findings.fix: Re-create the trace driver as a repo tool, e.g. a make v1-intc-sched target that regenerates the tables from the current core and diffs them against v1_intc_tb.cpp.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_intc.sv:237-239, 293 vs rtl/v1/v1_soc_pkg.sv irq_t.code comment ('stable while req')
findings.problem: irq.code follows the current winner while irq.req stays 1. The behaviour is correct for a priority INTC, and the core latches the code at the take, but the package contract says the code is stable while req.
findings.repro: adv --only B1. TMU1 at level 10 requesting (0x420); WDT ITI rises at level 12: code becomes 0x560 with req held at 1. B2: when ITI drops, the code goes back to 0x420 with req still 1.
findings.fix: Lead: reword irq_t.code to 'valid while req; sampled by the core at the take (SOC 4.3.4)'. No RTL change is needed.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_intc.sv:221-241 (a symmetric IMASK synchroniser); SOC 3.4 specifies only the lowering direction
findings.problem: Raising IMASK takes the same 9-10 cycles as lowering. This is unmeasured on the console, not marked [P], and not reported as a contract issue. A request above the old IMASK can be accepted with SR.IMASK already raised (KOS irq_disable). SOC 6.2's lockstep legality check (level > IMASK) would reject such an entry.
findings.repro: adv --only D1. TMU1 at level 10 rises at s-2 with IMASK 6; IMASK becomes 15 at s. irq.req is 1 from s+2/3 to s+8/9, i.e. a level-10 request presented with IMASK 15.
findings.fix: Mark it [P] in the RTL header and raise it as a contract issue. The lead then either records a legality window of s+10 for WI-REF or specifies an immediate raise path. It can be measured with a PH-style probe that lets a source rise just before irq_disable.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_excregs.sv:74-82 (else-if priority), comment at :19-20
findings.problem: A bus write that coincides with an excw pulse is dropped even when it targets a different register, although the slave acks it. The comment's argument that this cannot happen ignores the DMAC master: an on-chip leg to 0x1F000020-28 decodes to CCN_EXC in any cycle.
findings.repro: adv --only B4. excw writes EXPEVT = 0x0E0 while a DMAC write sets TRA = 0x3FC in the same cycle: TRA reads 0x000. excw writes INTEVT = 0x420 with a DMAC write EXPEVT = 0x555: EXPEVT reads 0x0E0.
findings.fix: Apply priority per register: the bus write lands unless excw writes that same register in this cycle.

findings.where: tb/bm/exceptions-intc/expected.json (INT=[0-9a-f]{3} in 69 of 73 exception records)
findings.problem: The [HW] rule 'INTEVT is kept across general exceptions' is checked by only one record that gates M1a (prio_irq_ill); the other 3 pinned records are board-only. A core whose excw.intr also writes INTEVT on some or all general exceptions passes almost every line.
findings.repro: python3 tb/bm/exceptions-intc/check.py agents/verify/WI-EXC/synthetic_intevt_bug.txt. This is the console log with the SoC stub lines and INT = EXP in all 60 records; excint reports only 1 failure (prio_irq_ill).
findings.fix: On the SoC, INTEVT is 000 after the POR until the first interrupt probe: pin INT=000 for records before C1. Otherwise add a relation 'INT equals the previous record's INT' for general-exception records.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_intc.sv:157-167 (one 4-bit noise canceller)
findings.problem: With IRLM = 1 the four pins are independent requests (hm Table 19.4). The RTL filters the 4-pin vector as one value, so a changing IRL3 keeps a steady IRL0 from ever being recognised. This is an unmarked [P] choice.
findings.repro: adv --only B3. IRLM = 1, IRL0 held low (level 13 > IMASK 12), IRL3 toggling every 2 Bcyc: irq.req is never 1 in 400 Icyc.
findings.fix: Mark it [P], or filter each pin separately when IRLM = 1.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_intc.sv:269-276
findings.problem: When software writes NMIB = 1 in the same cycle as nmi_ack, acceptance wins (NMIB = 0). This priority is not marked [P].
findings.repro: adv --only C8 prints ICR = 0000 after an NMIB = 1 write strobed in the nmi_ack cycle.
findings.fix: Add a [P] comment.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_cpg.sv:37-40 (WI-CLK) vs rtl/v1/v1_intc.sv wake = rq || ns
findings.problem: The CPG derives its 8-Icyc RESYNC from 'the INTC's wake changing right after a pce'. The INTC's wake becomes visible in ph-1 / ph-3 cycles, so the real RESYNC is 6 or 8 by phase. This matters for the M1a SLEEP wake cost (8-12 [HW]).
findings.repro: adv --only D2: a source rising at ph 0..3 makes wake visible 5 / 4 / 5 / 4 cycles later, in a ph-1 or ph-3 cycle, never ph 0.

verify:WI-P4.report:
I verified WI-P4 (`v1_p4bus.sv`, `v1_lsu.sv`) and do not accept it as delivered: two defects must be fixed first (F1, F2). The implementer's own checks all still pass.

**Implementer's checks, re-run:**
- `v1-p4bus` and `v1-lsu` pass; lint of both units is clean.
- Planted-bug runs: 19 of 19 caught for the bridge, 21 of 21 for the LSU.
- 8 extra random seeds at `--n 20000` pass.
- At `--n 30000` every seed fails, but only because the testbench stops after 200000 cycles (F6), not because of the RTL.

**My tests** are in `agents/verify/WI-P4/` (`make p4v`, `make lsuv`, `make seeds`, `make mutants`). They reuse the repo's flattened tops and slave stubs read-only.
- They reproduce the console's exact bracketed totals for every read measurement: timers-clock F and T rows, and the bsc-memmap T1/T8/T24 rows.
- They also cover: a decode comparison against the C++ model (6000 random addresses, no mismatch), random traffic with random CPU-only and manual resets, quadword accesses with DMAC traffic in between, DMAC ties, `err`, and posting across paths.
- 8 of 8 planted bugs are caught. One limitation: the timing rows only require the console value to be reachable at some Pclk phase, so they do not pin Bclk D1+D2 = 6 or WREL = 3. The implementer's tests pin those.

**Findings:**
- **F1 (bug).** After a CPU-only or manual reset lands on a CPU Iclk read that has already been captured, the path keeps a stale `orph` flag. The next Iclk write that is not stalled (CPU or DMAC) is strobed twice and takes 4 cycles instead of 3. A one-line fix, tested on a scratch copy, removes the problem and the implementer's tb still passes.
- **F2 (measured timing).** 16 back-to-back 32-bit Pclk writes between two PMCTR reads: the console measured 181 (timers-clock "≈ 11.1 per write"); the RTL gives 184 to 187 at every phase. The longword entry is released 3 cycles too late. Releasing the entry and freeing the bus for the next strobe need separate structures.
- **F3 (minor).** A loop of 8 × (16-bit write, 16-bit read of the same register): console 192, RTL 194 to 197. It needs one console probe under open question 9.13.
- **F4 (PMC event).** Event 0x09 does not count PREF. WI-DBG's new console survey shows that a PREF to the store queue does count (9 per iteration against the RTL's 8).
- **F5 (for the lead).** An MMUCR read produces no VOLRD record, but the MMU's C++ model marks MMUCR as time-dependent, so the reference model's lockstep check logs an error on every MMUCR read.
- **F6 (weak tests).** The implementer's tests have no "reset, then Iclk write" case, no resets in the random traffic, no check of the 16-access console totals, and a fixed cycle limit that breaks large random runs.
- **F7 (minor).** `bpost_bsc` is still 0 in the cycle a BSC or SDMR write enters the posting slot, so the BSC can start a bus cycle in that cycle before the register write lands.
- **F8 (for the lead).** The write record for a posted P4 write is emitted when the write is acked, but a manual reset can still drop it before it reaches the register.

Everything else I checked matches the contract: the port lists match §3.8 exactly, and decode, the stall rule, DMAC master and `err`, ordering, the §4.2 routing table and the MA port contract all hold. The implementer's question about CCR.OCE is answered: `v1_mmu` already folds OCE into `dxlat.c`.

No repo files were edited, no hardware was used, `make v1` was not needed, and nothing was committed. The full report is `agents/reports/units/WI-P4-verify.md`.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_p4bus.sv:326 (kill_ack) and :357 (orph set), module v1_p4bus_path
findings.problem: orph is set when rst.cpu (implied by rst.man) hits a CPU read that is already captured, and it is cleared only on the next acceptance. kill_ack = orph || ... also gates the ack of an Iclk write captured in its own acceptance cycle (imm && cap). That write is performed but not acked, the slot is freed, and the still-presenting master is accepted and strobed again. Result: two non-stalled strobes for one transaction (violates SOC.md 3.1.5) and occupancy 4 instead of 3. It affects CPU writes (CCR, MMUCR, UBC, PMCR, EXC) and DMAC 0x1F Iclk writes. A realistic trigger is a WDT manual reset while code polls a CCN register or PMCTR.
findings.repro: make -C agents/verify/WI-P4 p4v, group orph: CCR read captured in MA1; the next cycle, rst.cpu or rst.man for 8 cycles and the CPU withdraws; then a BARA write (CPU), a CCR write (CPU) or a 0x1F200000 write (DMAC). All 6 reset cases show 'extra strobes=1 occ=4'; the no-reset control shows 1 capture and occupancy 3. The randrst group (random traffic with random resets), seeds 1-3, finds 8 second strobes, all Iclk writes.
findings.fix: kill_ack = (orph && !acc) || (r_cpu && !(imm ? in_m : m)); (or clear orph when the slot empties). Verified on agents/scratch/WI-P4/fix_orph: orph and randrst seeds 1-4 pass, and v1-p4bus still passes. Add a reset-then-Iclk-write vector to tb/v1_p4bus_tb.cpp.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_p4bus.sv v1_p4bus_path release chain (rl / rel from lt = the second 16-bit transfer), for Pclk longword posted writes; header claim 'every target fits'
findings.problem: A 32-bit Pclk posted write frees its entry at strobe+9, so the next write is acked 3 Icyc later than on the console. timers-clock 3.0 'write 32 bit ≈ 11.1 Icyc' (tc.elf.hwlog: 16 x mov.l TCOR1 or TCNT1 between two PMCTR reads = 181) cannot be reproduced at any Pclk phase: the RTL gives 184-187. 16-bit writes match exactly (124). The arithmetic total = (strobe1 - a) + 14*12 + F + 1, with strobe1 - a >= 6, needs F = 6 (16-bit F = 5) while the strobe spacing stays 12. So releasing the entry and freeing the bus for the next strobe must be separate structures.
findings.repro: make -C agents/verify/WI-P4 p4v, group tcF, rows 'wr32 TCOR1' and 'wr32 TCNT1': RTL by phase {184,185,186,187}, console 181.
findings.fix: For a Pclk longword posted write, release the entry at strobe+6 and block the path's next strobe until the first pce >= strobe+9 (second transfer + WREL). This keeps 8/12 back to back, 64/96 per 8 in loops, 3 isolated, wr16 124 and write->read 23..26, and gives 181. Add the tc F 16-access brackets to v1-p4bus timing.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_lsu.sv:117 (pmc_ev[PMC_OP_ALL] uses xfer, which excludes DK_PREF)
findings.problem: Event 0x09 (all operand accesses) does not count PREF. Console: tools/hw/debug-ubc-hudi/pmcsurvey.out row 'Q 09' (WI-DBG 9.6 survey, 2026-09-23 08:15): sqw (4 SQ stores) = 256/64 = 4 per iteration; sqpref (8 SQ stores + pref @r5) = 576/64 = 9 per iteration. So a PREF to the SQ counts once, consistent with debug-ubc-hudi 4.7 'every operand access of any kind'. The [P] choice in the header contradicts this.
findings.repro: make -C agents/verify/WI-P4 lsuv, group ev09: sqw RTL 4 = console 4; sqpref RTL 8, console 9.
findings.fix: Count DK_PREF in 0x09 at its ack (at least on the RG_SQ route; OC and P4 routes [P]); update p4bus_ref.h lsu_ev_op_all to match. OCBx and TAS purge remain unmeasured.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_p4bus.sv Pclk path (write -> read of the same path locks at 24 per pair)
findings.problem: tc.elf.hwlog line 83: PMCTR ; 8 x (mov.w -> TCR1 ; mov.w TCR1 ->) ; PMCTR = 192 on the console; the RTL gives 194-197 at every phase. After the first pair the RTL phase-locks at 24 per pair. The console's 189 over 8 pairs, with the first pair >= 23 (tc2 T: other module 26), needs later pairs averaging below 24, which no pce-aligned acceptance structure produces. The only difference from the passing isolated T row is same register (F) against another module (T). This number is only in the log, not in a spec table.
findings.repro: make -C agents/verify/WI-P4 p4v, group tcF, row 'wr16/rd16 TCR1 pair (x8)': RTL {194,195,196,197}, console 192.
findings.fix: Settle under 9.13 with one console probe (the x8 pair loop with the read to another module, and an isolated T-style pair to the same register), then calibrate. No RTL change is proposed until then.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_lsu.sv:102-104 (VOLRD rule, per SOC.md 6.3) vs tb/mmu_ref.h:441 and tb/sh4_sys.h:1305
findings.problem: CONTRACT ISSUE for the lead. WI-MMU's model marks MMUCR (CCN 0x10) volatile ('LRUI follows speculative fetches'), and Sh4Sys lockstep logs an error for a volatile register not covered by the VOLRD rule. The SOC.md 6.3 rule (implemented exactly by v1_lsu) has no CCN_MMU term, so every MMUCR read (for example a read-modify-write of MMUCR) stops the lockstep checker.
findings.repro: make -C agents/verify/WI-P4 lsuv, group mmucr: an MMUCR load (0xFF000010) produces no record; a TSTR load produces a VOLRD record (kind 6). In sh4_sys.h vol_read, logged=false with vol=true pushes 'is_volatile register ... is not covered by the VOLRD rule'.
findings.fix: The lead decides: either SOC.md 6.3 adds 'reads of MMUCR' (then v1_lsu adds blk == P4B_CCN_MMU && base[7:0] == 8'h10 to vol, and p4bus_ref.h lsu_volatile / sh4_sys.h volrd_p4 match), or WI-MMU drops the volatile flag.

findings.where: tb/v1_p4bus_tb.cpp (t_reset, t_random, t_timing), tb/p4bus_ref.h lsu_ev_op_all
findings.problem: The implementer's tests cannot catch F1 to F4. No reset case is followed by an Iclk write, and random traffic never resets. The timing group checks only the SOC.md table values (8/12 back to back, 96 per loop), not the console's 16-access brackets (181/124/320/256) or the pair loop (192). The 0x09 PREF choice is pinned by the tb's own [P] predicate. Also, t_random uses a fixed run(200000) budget, so 'v1-p4bus --n 30000' fails at every seed with 'run did not finish' (a testbench limit, not the RTL).
findings.repro: build/obj_v1_p4bus/tb --seed 21 --n 30000 prints 'run did not finish (cyc 200012)' and 'v1-p4bus: FAIL (9649)'; the same seed with --n 20000 passes. The p4v and lsuv groups above fail while v1-p4bus and v1-lsu pass.
findings.fix: Add a reset-then-Iclk-write vector and random resets (as agents/verify/WI-P4 randrst), the tc F / tc2 T / bsc-memmap bracket rows (as the tcF / tcT / bsc groups), and the pmcsurvey 0x09 rows; scale the run budget with n.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_p4bus.sv:241-242 (bpost_bsc = slot_v[1] && ...)
findings.problem: bpost_bsc rises only the cycle after a BSC or SDMR posted write enters the Bclk entry; the implementer's tb pins the interval [ack+1, capture+4]. When the ack cycle is a bce cycle, the BSC can accept a CPU or DMAC bus request in that cycle, before the MCR or SDMR write lands. This matches the letter of SOC.md 3.1.5 ('while the entry holds') but not its intent (boot stub MCR/SDMR3 then SDRAM).
findings.repro: tb/v1_p4bus_tb.cpp final_checks: iv = {tack + 1, tcap + 4}; bpost_bsc is 0 in the ack cycle of any BSC/SDMR write (for example t_post w4 / w6).
findings.fix: bpost_bsc |= the Bclk path's posted_w of a BSC / SDMR2 / SDMR3 write in its acceptance cycle.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_lsu.sv:107-110 (MEMW at the ack) with v1_p4bus manual-reset drop (droppable)
findings.problem: CONTRACT NOTE for the lead. The MEMW record of a posted P4 write is emitted at its posted ack (MA3), but SOC.md 2.3 / 3.1.6 make the bridge drop an un-strobed posted entry on a manual reset. A write to a register the manual reset holds (BSC, STBCR, DMAC SAR/DAR) is then in the checker's write set but never performed. The window is 1-4 cycles after the ack.
findings.repro: tb/v1_p4bus_tb.cpp t_reset case (c): an IPRB posted write acked, then rst.man before its strobe; the slave never sees it (IPRB 0000), while the LSU would already have logged MEMW for it.
findings.fix: The lead states which wins: either do not drop posted entries on a manual reset (complete them), or have the checker discard MEMW records of posted P4 writes caught by a manual reset.

contract_issues: SOC.md §2.2 has v1_soc latch md[8:0] 'at the end of rst.pin', but v1_cpg loads FRQCR from its md input during rst.pin. WI-SOC must drive v1_cpg.md from the md pins directly, or from a latch that is transparent while rst.pin. Otherwise the first power-on reset loads a stale or zero latch: mode 0 gives FRQCR 0x0E1A, so Bclk = Pclk = Iclk/4.

v1_cpg takes sleep_req on its rising edge. A level held through the sleep and a one-cycle pulse both work, but the core must drop it at least once between two SLEEPs (for example when it takes the wake-up interrupt). SOC.md §4.4.3 only says 'asserts'; WI-CORE-A should know this.
dmac_run already includes !STBCR.MSTP4, as the spec's v1_cpg sketch has it. The 'run = dmac_run & !MSTP4' in the SOC.md §3.8 v1_dmac comment is therefore redundant but harmless.
[P] A posted FRQCR write that drains while the CPU is already asleep changes FRQCR without a PLL-relock SETTLE, because a settle starts only from RUN. This never happens on the DC.
open_questions: Spec 9.1: TMU register access while MSTP2 = 1 stays [P] (reads 0, writes ignored). I did not measure it: the spec says the bus might hang, and the hardware rule forbids tests that can hang the console.

Manual-only behaviour that cannot be measured safely on a DC: deep sleep, standby and its WDT settle, FRQCR/PLL relock (including restarting the second phase from WTCNT), watchdog-mode resets, TCLK, input capture, RTC oscillator timing (PEF/CF), wake with BL = 1.

The timing tolerances in tb/bm/timers-clock/expected.json (F/T within 1 Icyc per access, B/D within 32-64, J/S windows) are my choice around the console numbers. WI-SOC may tighten them at M1b once WI-P4's synchroniser depths (SOC.md 9.13) are final.

Remaining [P] choices: the 8-Icyc reset stretch; STATUS = normal during a CPU-only reset; the RTC register size rule; TCPR2 and the RTC counters start at 0 in simulation; MD 110/111 treated as mode 5; prohibited divider codes treated as x1/8.
impl:WI-CLK.notes:
Resumed after the crash. The previous agent's five RTL units, C++ model and five testbenches were sound; I read them all against SOC.md and the spec and re-ran every check. I finished what was missing and fixed three things:
(1) v1_rstc could not recover from some power-up states: a kind value outside the five codes won every merge, so a held RESET never became a pin POR. It no longer merges, and make v1-rstc now also runs 8 random power-up states.
(2) Two unbounded wait loops made the wdt-rate mutant hang the WDT testbench; it was only counted as caught because I killed the process. I bounded every wait loop, and the mutant script now counts a 300 s timeout as a failure.
(3) The bare-metal suite had no Makefile, expected values or checker. I added the Makefile, mkexpected.py/expected.json and check.py, finished the ISS runner, and added the umbrella targets in tb/mk/v1_clk.mk (v1-clk, v1-clk-lint, v1-clk-mutants, v1-clk-bm, v1-clk-bm-k).

One safe hardware run, tools/hw/timers-clock/tc4.c (exit 0, every register restored), settled spec 9.5 and 9.6 and three [P] choices, all matching the RTL as written:
- WOVF written as 1 sets it.
- RCR2.RTCEN (not START) gates the alarm comparator.
- The day carries when day >= the month's length; invalid BCD and out-of-range fields follow the RTL's rule.
- ADJ uses the START bit written with it.
Its console lines are now verbatim checks in v1_rtc_tb and v1_wdt_tb, and a fifth bare-metal program (tb/bm/timers-clock/tc4.c).

make v1 was not run: WI-CLK's files are not in its file set, and the work item does not ask for it. WI-REF's tb/sh4_sys.h already uses sh4t::Sh4Timers. Scratch logs are in agents/scratch/WI-CLK/. Build products are in build/ (bm images, bmrun, v1_clk_mut).

verify:WI-DBG.report:
agents/reports/units/WI-DBG-verify.md

I found no functional bug in the four units. v1_ubc, v1_perfctr, v1_hudi and v1_ccn_id match the spec, hm section 20 and every console number I could replay. That includes a new replay behind the real v1_p4bus (WI-P4), wired by the SOC.md §3.1.2 port table, which gives pm_lat 0 3 6 9 / 21 21 21 21 end to end, plus the p4probe D/S/M/W/H/U/I and ubcbrk A lines.

What I ran:
- All of the implementer's claims reproduce: make v1-dbg, v1-dbg-lint, 34/34 mutants, v1-dbg-bm.
- New independent testbenches in agents/verify/WI-DBG/, with references written from the manual and spec, not from tb/sh4_dbg.h:
  - vt_ubc: 54.7 M checks plus 3 seeds.
  - vt_pmc: 10 M checks plus 2 seeds, including the carry into H and the 2^48 wrap through a preloaded counter.
  - vt_small: every offset, size and read/write of the CCN id and H-UDI.
  - vt_int: the units behind the real bridge.
- 40 of 40 planted bugs are caught by my testbenches: the implementer's 34 plus 6 new ones.
- The settle section alone rejects IF_DLY 2 and 4. I checked this with a copy of their tb whose model delay matches the RTL's, so only the console points can fail.

Findings:
1. Minor: a SEQ=0 write in the same cycle as a channel-A hit leaves a stale "A seen". A later SEQ=1 write then lets the next B match break with no new A.
2. Contract (implementer also reported it, I confirm): ubc_ctl_t needs seq and pre_armed. Without them v1_ubc does not match its §3.8 port list.
3. Contract: SOC.md never says what the core presents on ubc_opq for each access kind. WI-CORE-A already presents the TAS.B purge (dk_ctl includes DK_TAS_PURGE), while v1_ubc's header says the purge presents nothing.
4. Contract/open (9.5): SOC.md §4.1 item 5's premise cannot hold. With the frozen 4-halfword queue, IF_DLY 3 and IF_DLY 4 each fit 42 of 44 console points. The choice of 3 rests on a 5-6 halfword run-ahead that has not been decided. The lead has to decide.
5. Weak test: the bare-metal "functional" check skips every deterministic p4probe P line except the PMCR read-back.
6. Minor: a default-constructed dbg::Ubc used functionally never fires instruction breaks.
7. Minor: report §6.4 says the core "needs" to take the operand tag in its last EX cycle. The console data does not require it: any EX cycle gives the same 7 points.
8. Minor: v1_hudi answers hit=1 at 0xFFF00002/3, which are not SDIR lanes.

Acceptance: met, except for finding 1 and the 9.5 / port-list items, which need the lead to change SOC.md.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_ubc.sv lines 338-355 (and tb/sh4_dbg.h Ubc::clock, same ordering)
findings.problem: A BRCR write with SEQ=0 lands in the same cycle as a channel-A hit taken under the old SEQ=1. The later non-blocking 'a_seen <= 1' overrides the write's clear, so a_seen stays 1 while SEQ=0. A later write of SEQ=1 re-arms channel B at once (b_live=1), and the next B match breaks and sets CMFB with no A since the re-enable. Manual 20.3.3(4): writing 0 to SEQ clears the pending A match.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-DBG/vt_ubc.cpp sec_seq_race (run.sh ubc): BRCR<-0008; {BRCR<-0000 and hit_a in the same cycle}; BRCR<-0008 -> ctl.b_live=1; hit_b -> event 0x1A=1, BRCR=4008. Logged in vt_ubc.log ('seq race' lines).
findings.fix: Give the SEQ=0 write priority for a_seen. Either clear a_seen every cycle while SEQ=0 ('if (!seq) a_seen <= 0'), or gate the set with '!(q_wr && q_reg==R_BRCR && !q_wm[3])'. Make the same change in dbg::Ubc::clock/reach.

findings.where: v1_soc_pkg.sv ubc_ctl_t / SOC.md 3.8 v1_ubc port list, 1.3.2 v1_fetch.ubc_pre_armed, 4.1 item 7
findings.problem: v1_ubc adds two outputs (ctl_seq, ctl_pre_armed) beyond its SOC.md 3.8 port list. Both are necessary. SEQ cannot be derived from b_live: SEQ=0 and (SEQ=1, A seen) both give b_live=1, yet channel A breaks only in the first case (hm 20.3.3(4)). v1_fetch.ubc_pre_armed has no other possible driver. So the unit does not 'match its 3.8 port list exactly' (8.2 integration rule). The implementer already reported this; I confirm it.
findings.repro: Compare v1_ubc.sv lines 70-96 with SOC.md 3.8. Case table: SEQ=0 -> b_live=1, A breaks; SEQ=1 with A seen -> b_live=1, A must not break (vt_ubc sec_seq, ubcbrk seq_AB BRCR 4009).
findings.fix: Lead: add 'seq' and 'pre_armed' to ubc_ctl_t (and SOC.md 3.8), and name v1_ubc as the driver of ubc_pre_armed in 4.1 item 7. v1_ubc then moves the two outputs into ctl.

findings.where: SOC.md 3.8 / v1_soc_pkg ubc_opq_t (per-kind mapping only in the v1_ubc.sv header); rtl/v1/v1_core.sv ~line 1008 (WI-CORE-A)
findings.problem: SOC.md does not define what the core presents on ubc_opq for each dkind. WI-DBG's rule lives only in the header of v1_ubc.sv: the TAS.B purge presents nothing, MOVCA.L carries data, PREF/OCB* are size L with nodata=1. WI-CORE-A already contradicts it: ubc_opq.nodata = dk_ctl(dk), and dk_ctl includes DK_TAS_PURGE, so once step A2 adds the purge micro-op it is presented as a read access. Also, the spec (4.1) lists MOVCA.L as having no data, while manual 20.3.1 / 20.3.5(3) do not (the implementer reported this and follows the manual).
findings.repro: BBRA=0x24 (operand, read, any size) and BARA = a TAS.B operand address. With the core's drive, the purge micro-op matches opm.a as well as the locked read: two tags on one instruction, event 0x19 counted twice, and the operand-break tag on micro-op 0. Code: v1_core.sv 'nodata: dk_ctl(ex_res[l].dk)' against v1_ubc.sv header lines 36-40.
findings.fix: Lead: add a per-dkind table to SOC.md 3.8 / the ubc_opq_t comment: v, wr, size, nodata and dq for LD, ST, PREF, OCBI/OCBP/OCBWB, MOVCA, RMW_RD/WR, TAS_PURGE/RD/WR and FMOV quad. Resolve the MOVCA.L data question in the spec, and align dk_ctl use in v1_core or v1_ubc's header.

findings.where: SOC.md 4.1 item 5 and 9.5; rtl/v1/v1_ubc.sv IF_DLY
findings.problem: SOC.md 4.1 item 5 says 'The UBC settle boundaries are met through the UBC's fetch-side copy delay' with v1's frozen 4-halfword queue. That cannot hold. NOP k=13's target (fetched at store MA3+4) breaks, while ADD k=9/10's target, also fetched at MA3+4, does not. No fetch-time copy delay can separate them. With the frozen queue, IF_DLY=3 and IF_DLY=4 tie at 42/44 console points (3 misses ADD 9/10, 4 misses NOP 13/14). IF_DLY=3 is chosen only on the undecided hypothesis of a 5-6 halfword run-ahead (44/44). So 9.5 is calibrated but not uniquely closed.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-DBG/run.sh settle: settle_ifdly3.log shows 44/44/42 at run-ahead 5/6/4; settle_ifdly4.log shows 42/40/42. Hand schedule: NOP word n fetched at W+n-3; ADD (4-halfword queue) word n fetched at 2n-1 with W=5, so ADD k=9/10 -> W+4.
findings.fix: Lead: decide the fetch run-ahead (WI-CORE-B), or settle it with one hardware probe of the fetch run-ahead after a P4 store. Then fix SOC.md 4.1 item 5 and the WI-DBG acceptance text. Keep IF_DLY=3 meanwhile and expect the M1b ubcevt S ADD 9/10 mismatch.

findings.where: tb/bm/debug-ubc-hudi/expected/p4probe.json (mkexpected.py classification)
findings.problem: Every p4probe P line except the PMCR read-back is classed 'env' and never compared, including tokens any correct implementation must reproduce. 'P run 0023/4023/8023' is all zeros (the PMEN & PMST rule). 'P ctr-write' has L/H = 0 after a clear (PMCTR read-only). 'P sizes' has PMCR2 r32/r8/r8+1 = 0 (the size rule). These PMC rules therefore have no program-level (M1b bm) check; only the unit tb covers them.
findings.repro: python3 over expected/p4probe.json: the P lines have class=env with why='values depend on the KOS build's C code...', although the run 0023/4023/8023 values are 0 regardless of the code.
findings.fix: Class those lines 'functional' and add 'ignore' entries for the cycle-dependent tokens (after-spin counts, cont/clr-running numbers, PMCTR2L r16 values).

findings.where: tb/sh4_dbg.h dbg::Ubc constructor 'explicit Ubc(int dly = 3)'
findings.problem: A default-constructed Ubc used functionally (P4Slave::wr and pre/post with no clock(), so 'now' stays 0) queues every fetch-side-copy write for cycle 4 and never applies it. Instruction breaks then never fire. sh4_sys.h and run_iss.cpp pass -1 today, so nothing is wrong yet, but the default is a trap for the next functional user.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-DBG/vt_model_default.cpp (g++ -std=c++17 -I tb): arm BBRA=0x14 on a PC, call pre(PC) 100 times -> 'default: NEVER fires', '-1: fires' (vt_model_default.log).
findings.fix: Default to -1 (functional), or apply writes to the copy at once when !cycle_mode.

findings.where: agents/reports/units/WI-DBG-impl.md section 6 item 4; v1_ubc.sv header lines 32-34
findings.problem: The report says the console's operand-settle boundary 'needs the core to take the tag in the cycle the micro-op leaves EX'. The data does not require this. For k<=2 NOPs the load is in EX at W-2..W (all before the write lands), and for k=3 its only EX cycle is W+1. Sampling opm in the first, any or the last EX cycle gives the same 7 points. The wording over-constrains WI-CORE-A.
findings.repro: Hand schedule (t_soK in ubcevt_s.s under v1's rules): k=0..2 load EX t=3..5 with W=5; k=3 load EX t=6. All give break iff k>=3.
findings.fix: Reword to 'consistent with sampling in any EX cycle'. No RTL change.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_hudi.sv line 183 (o[17:2]==0)
findings.problem: A byte or halfword strobe at 0xFFF00002/0xFFF00003 answers hit=1, but SDIR is a 16-bit register at 0xFFF00000-01, so these offsets are holes. SOC.md 3.1.2 says hit=0 for any offset that is not a register. rdata is correctly 0, and the bridge treats hit as informational.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-DBG/vt_small.log 'note: hudi hit=1 at offset 00002 size 1 / 00003 size 0'.
findings.fix: Decode SDIR with o[17:1]==0. Optional: the effect is informational only.

verify:WI-MMU.report:
WI-MMU verification: the MMU is correct in every steady-state rule I tested, but I found one contract conflict, three refill races and two minor issues. I edited no repo files. Report: agents/reports/units/WI-MMU-verify.md.

**Implementer's targets.** All re-run in a private build dir, and all reproduce as reported:
- lint clean, including in the full SOC.md 1.4 package order;
- `make v1-mmu`: 5.89M checks, 0 failed, all 12 model mutations caught;
- seed 777 with 2M vectors: 11.0M checks, 0 failed;
- `make v1-mmu-plant`: 21 of 21 plants caught;
- `make v1-mmu-bm`: 1040 of 1301 records compared, 0 mismatches, and `expect.json` regenerates byte-identically;
- the bm port can fail: three of my planted RTL copies give 29, 49 and 120 mismatches.

**My testbench** (agents/verify/WI-MMU/):
- `vtop.sv` wraps both `v1_mmu` builds plus the real `v1_rstc`, so the multiple-hit reset chain runs end to end.
- `spec_model.h` is an independent model written from mmu.md, SOC.md and hm, not from `tb/mmu_ref.h`.
- `vtb.cpp` covers resets and the reset chain, the register size rule and same-cycle collisions, and array bit maps with junk address bits. It also runs an exhaustive data matrix (32k vectors), random and concurrency sweeps (300k data, 100k fetches, 150k lookups during refills) and races of every writer against the refill FSM.
- `plant.sh`: 18 of 18 plants caught.
- Result: 0 unexpected failures on 3 seeds, and 8 finding tags reproduced.

**Findings.**
- **FIND-1 (contract conflict).** After a multiple-hit reset PTEH reads 0. hm 5.6.1 and the SOC.md 2.3 note say it keeps the VPN and the pre-exception ASID; the SOC.md 2.3 table clears it on manual reset. `tb/mmu_ref.h` does the same, so a lockstep run cannot see it.
- **FIND-2 to FIND-4 (refill races).** The refill is not atomic against UTLB writers. A TI in RF_SRCH or RF_RD, an LDTLB in RF_SRCH, or an associative invalidate captured in RF_WR leaves a stale or mixed valid ITLB entry.
- **FIND-5 (minor).** An MMU-0 build still exports `at` = 1 when software sets AT, so `v1_sq` would send SQ bursts to the identity address.
- **FIND-6 (minor).** The ITLBFILL record is still emitted when a same-cycle array write or TI overrides the refill's write.

**Implementer's contract issues.** All four are confirmed in the code:
- `ma_commit` needs qualifying: the core pulses it for every access (`v1_core.sv:699`, `:827`).
- SOC.md's `xl_stall` rule would deadlock: `dex.v` stays high while the access is held in EX.
- `dxlat_t.c` includes CCR.OCE; SOC.md should say so.
- The MMU commit records carry ISN 0; WI-SOC must stamp them.

**Acceptance.** MMU-0 and MMU-1 are met at unit level. Before M2, the lead must settle FIND-1; FIND-2 to FIND-4 are recommended fixes.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu_regs.sv:85-86 (rst.man branch); tb/mmu_ref.h:133-134 (reset_man); SOC.md 2.3 table vs 2.3 note
findings.problem: After a TLB multiple-hit reset, PTEH reads 0. The core's excw (or arr_mhit's cap_v) writes PTEH.VPN in the request cycle, but v1_rstc then holds rst.man for 8 Icyc and v1_mmu_regs clears pteh_vpn and pteh_asid under it. hm 5.6.1 (4)/(5) (TLB_multi_hit: PTEH.VPN = PAGE_NUMBER; the ASID stays the one at the exception) and the SOC.md 2.3 note both require PTEH to be set. The SOC.md 2.3 table says 0 [P]. The model has the same rule, so a lockstep run cannot catch it.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU/run.sh gives FIND-1-mhit-pteh: PTEH=00000000, want 4c0b3055 (excw tea 4C0B3124 + mhit_req, PTEH.ASID 55). It also gives FIND-1-assoc-pteh: PTEH=00000000, want 2a000421 (associative double hit -> arr_mhit -> v1_rstc). TEA is correct in both.
findings.fix: Hold PTEH (VPN and ASID) through a manual reset. hm Appendix A gives PTEH as Undefined on a manual reset, so holding it is legal. Change the SOC.md 2.3 row to 'PTEH held' and make mmu_ref.h reset_man match. The alternative, clearing only when rst_code != RC_140, needs rst_code as a new v1_mmu input.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_core.sv:699,827 vs SOC.md 3.8 ma_commit / mmu 3.6 (implementer's contract issue 1, confirmed)
findings.problem: arch = v && dk != DK_NONE for every access, and ma_commit = lreq.v && lrsp.ack && lreq.arch. v1_mmu steps URC on every pulse, so wired directly, P1, P2 and AT=0 accesses, PREF outside the SQ, and SQ stores whose TLB check failed would all advance URC, against HW D1/R4/S. The interim qualification mmu_urc_counts(lreq, at, ora) reads AT in MA rather than EX. It therefore also counts an access that was untranslated in EX and acked after an AT 0->1 write lands; that is inside the manual's 4-instruction window.
findings.repro: Code reading of v1_core.sv lines 699 and 827. At unit level, every ma_commit pulse steps URC (v1_mmu_tb t_urc; my L2/L3 tags).
findings.fix: Add a 'cnt' bit to dxlat_t, driven by v1_mmu in EX and latched with the micro-op, and set ma_commit = lreq.v & lrsp.ack & lreq.arch & lreq.x.cnt (lead + WI-CORE-A). Until then v1_soc should AND in mmu_urc_counts.

findings.where: SOC.md 3.8 xl_stall rule vs rtl/v1/v1_core.sv:1001-1008 (implementer's contract issue 2, confirmed)
findings.problem: SOC.md says xl_stall is 1 while the EX access uses the UTLB CAM. The core drives dex.v=1 for an access micro-op held in EX by mah. An OC associative array write (an MA bridge access) followed by any memory instruction would therefore stall forever. The RTL's separate EX compare port D, with xl_stall only in RF_SRCH, avoids this. The refill FSM never waits on the array, so nothing starves.
findings.repro: Code reading: v1_core.sv dex block (lines 1001-1008) and the mah hold in SOC.md 3.2.2. agents/verify/WI-MMU tags K1-K3 (150k data lookups and 29k array reads during refills, at most 3 stalls) confirm the RTL's alternative behaves.
findings.fix: The lead should rewrite the SOC.md 3.8 xl_stall rule to match the RTL: xl_stall only in the refill's UTLB search cycle, with the data side on its own compare port.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu.sv:327-328 (the refill latches rf_any in RF_SRCH and rf_ent in RF_RD; nothing checks TI)
findings.problem: A MMUCR write with TI=1 that lands while the refill is in RF_SRCH or RF_RD does not stop the refill. RF_WR writes a V=1 ITLB entry copied from a UTLB entry that TI has just invalidated, so a translation survives TI. TI in RF_WR or later is handled correctly.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU/run.sh gives FIND-2-ti-SRCH and FIND-2-ti-RD. Setup: UTLB 7 maps 40010000, AT=1, fetch 40010000 misses at cycle m, and an MMUCR<-5 capture lands at m+1 or m+2. Result: ITLB valid mask 8, UTLB 7 V=0, and the retry hits. Compliant code cannot reach this, because the manual puts MMUCR writes in P1/P2 code with a P0 branch at least 8 instructions later.
findings.fix: Add a flop set by ti while rf_st is RF_SRCH or RF_RD and cleared at IDLE, and gate rf_iwe and tap[1].v with its inverse. The retry then misses, and the new refill finds the UTLB invalid and returns a UTLB miss.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu.sv:200,328 (RF_RD reads UTLB[rf_uidx] one cycle after the RF_SRCH match)
findings.problem: An LDTLB (ldtlb=1) in the refill's RF_SRCH cycle with URC equal to the matched entry overwrites that entry at the end of SRCH. RF_RD then copies the new entry, and the ITLB ends up with VPN from the fetch VA but PPN, SZ and PR from an unrelated page. No serial order of refill and LDTLB produces that mistranslation.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU/run.sh gives FIND-3-ldtlb-race. Setup: UTLB 7 maps 40010000->0C010000, URC=7, PTEH/PTEL = VPN 50000000 -> PPN 0D000000, and ldtlb is pulsed in RF_SRCH. The fetch of 40010000 is acked with if_pa 0D000000.
findings.fix: Latch port A's ua_ent (the matching entry) in RF_SRCH together with ua_idx. That is the pre-write data a synchronous read at the end of SRCH would return, so it fits the RF_RD comment.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu.sv:186 (the UTLB array stall covers RF_SRCH and RF_RD only), with :190 (i_as uses the current ITLB)
findings.problem: An associative UTLB address-array write with AT=1 whose first strobe falls in the refill's search is captured in RF_WR. Its ITLB-side compare runs on the ITLB before the refill's write and misses the entry being installed. Its UTLB side clears V of the entry the refill has already read. The result is UTLB V=0 but ITLB V=1 for the same page, although the associative write must invalidate both (hm 3.7.4). A plain DA1/AA write in RF_WR giving a stale copy is legal ITLB non-coherence and is not part of this finding.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU/run.sh gives FIND-4-assoc-race. Setup: UTLB 7 maps 40010000, AT=1, fetch misses at m, and an associative write of 40010000 (V=0) starts at m+1. It stalls twice, captures at m+3, and leaves ITLB valid mask 8; the retry hits.
findings.fix: Add RF_WR to the UTLB array stall: arr_is_u && rf_st in {RF_SRCH, RF_RD, RF_WR}.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu.sv:127 (at = mmucr.at also for TRANSLATE=0); rtl/v1/v1_sq.sv:91
findings.problem: In MMU-0 the at output follows MMUCR.AT while dxl stays the identity. v1_sq chooses bpa = at ? x.pa : QACR, so an MMU-0 build that has set AT sends SQ bursts to va[28:0] (area 0) instead of the QACR area, and the core's future EX checks see an MMU that says 'on'. No boot target sets AT.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU/run.sh gives FIND-5-mmu0-at: after MMUCR<-1, an SQ store to E0000040 has at0=1, rg=RG_SQ and pa=00000040.
findings.fix: assign at = TRANSLATE ? mmucr.at : 1'b0 (MMUCR still reads back AT), or add a SOC.md note that TRANSLATE=0 builds never set AT.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu.sv:341 (tap[1].v = rf_iwe)
findings.problem: In the RF_WR cycle a software ITLB array write to the victim wins over the refill ([P]), and so does TI. The CK_ITLBFILL record is still emitted, so a lockstep model that injects it (SOC.md 6.2) would hold an ITLB entry the RTL does not have.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU/run.sh gives FIND-6-fill-record in both variants. With an ITLB AA write to e3 captured in RF_WR: record 1, but ITLB e3 AA = 12345000 (the software value). The TI-in-RF_WR variant behaves the same way.
findings.fix: Qualify tap[1].v with !(i_aw && aw_idx==rf_victim) && !ti, or state in the SOC.md 6.3 record semantics that the ITLBFILL record is applied before same-cycle array writes and TI.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu.sv:336-343 commit records (implementer's contract issue 4, confirmed)
findings.problem: LDTLB and ITLBFILL records carry isn=0 because v1_mmu has no ISN input. SOC.md 6.3 requires the instruction's ISN.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU tag L6-isn: tap0_isn = tap1_isn = 0.
findings.fix: WI-SOC stamps the ISNs: LDTLB with the ISN of the LDTLB micro-op in MA, ITLBFILL with tap.core.next_isn. Alternatively add an isn input to v1_mmu, which is a SOC.md port change.

findings.where: tb/v1_mmu_tb.cpp (sections refill/regs), tb/mmu_ref.h
findings.problem: The unit testbench never drives a UTLB writer (TI, LDTLB, associative or array write) concurrently with an in-flight ITLB refill, and never runs the multiple-hit reset through v1_rstc. That is how FIND-1 to FIND-4 escaped. The random section checks the RTL only against a model by the same author, which shares the manual-reset PTEH choice.
findings.repro: Apply the agents/verify/WI-MMU FIND-2/3/4 scenarios to tb/v1_mmu_tb.cpp: all its sections still pass on the current RTL.
findings.fix: Add the race scenarios (TI / LDTLB / associative write at m+1..m+3 of a refill) and a v1_rstc chain check to tb/v1_mmu_tb, each with a planted-bug counterpart, once the RTL fixes land.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_mmu.sv:281-283 (PREF conversion also covers FX_MHIT)
findings.problem: A PREF outside the SQ that multiple-hits in the UTLB is dropped silently (fx NONE, RG_P4RSV). pm 10.73 says a PREF error is a NOP; hm 3.6.4 says every data TLB multiple hit resets. Both are [P] readings; it is a question for the lead, not a defect.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-MMU tag X2-pref-mhit (two overlapping UTLB entries at 50000000; a PREF gives fx 0 and rg 6, a load gives FX_MHIT).
findings.fix: The lead decides: keep the NOP, or report FX_MHIT for PREF too.

IMASK raise: SOC 3.4 specifies only the lowering latency. The RTL uses the same synchroniser in both directions [P], so after IMASK is raised at s, an already-presented request stays up to s+8 (s even) or s+9 (s odd) and falls at s+9 / s+10. The lead must choose one of two: (a) WI-REF's lockstep legality check (SOC 6.2) allows entries with level <= the new IMASK before s+10, or (b) SOC specifies an immediate raise path. contract_issues: breq_t.lock is documented as TAS only. The DMAC also sets it on the read of a dual-address unit whose write goes to the BSC (hm 14.3.4 bus-locks the pair). SOC.md 3.3's no-hand-over list should add the DMAC dual unit, and WI-BSC must honour lock on dma_bq.

Cycle steal: between units the DMAC drops dma_bq.v for exactly 2 Bclk (REL, IDLE), and WI-BSC must grant a waiting CPU request in that window (dmac2 T5 strict alternation). In burst mode the next request is on the port in the Bclk after done, so the BSC sees no gap.

Single-address pipelining: the DMAC keeps bq.v up with up to 4 accepted single cycles outstanding (tracked only for DACK/TDACK/ID), so the BSC sets the pipelining depth. The measured 5.77 Bcyc per 32-byte CH2 unit (dmac1 S13) is WI-BSC's calibration target.

Single-address device->memory writes: the DMAC drives no bwd data (the board supplies it via xb_rdata, SOC 3.3.3). TDACK/DACK are asserted in the bce of each wd_req, so the manual's '2 cycles before the data' depends on how far the BSC's wd_req leads the beat [P].

DMAC P4 accesses [P]: a DMAC access to its own register block reads 0 and ignores the write; a quadword on-chip leg is two longword transactions at a and a+4; a 32-byte unit or a non-0x1F address on an on-chip leg is class B with no transaction.

SOC 3.1.5 'the DMAC presents on bce cycles': p4q is a Bclk flop that rises in the Icyc after a bce and holds until ack; the ack may come in any Icyc and is consumed at the next bce. This matches what WI-P4 built.

Manual reset of an in-flight unit (SOC 2.3): its counter update is applied without TE or AE, CHCR/DMAOR read 0, no unit is accepted while rst.man is asserted, and the DDT queues and request state are emptied.
dreq_t levels pass through one Bclk register, so a module must hold its level until the DMAC's own data-register access (p4s_req_t.dma) clears it.
open_questions: SOC.md 9.10 (which CPU access during a DMAC burst hangs the chip, dmac3): not run, because it needs a human ready to reset the console. The RTL models no hang; a CPU bus access waits for the release.

M3 timing calibration with the real BSC: burst 46.26 Icyc/unit, cycle steal 50.0-50.6 (52.2 while polling), CH2 single address 5.77 Bcyc/unit, one-unit start-to-poll minimum 89 Icyc. The DMAC's share is fixed by structure. The tb/bm/dmac timing tolerances are my choice [P].

Spec §9 items that remain unmeasured and are modelled as [P] (listed in the report §6/§7): burst preemption, SCI/SCIF with TM=1, flag-arming details, class-B junk values (0x04040404 is not reproduced), prohibited codes, carry into SAR/DAR bits 31:29, notes 17/19.
The board for the bm ports must read SB_MDST (0xA05F6C18) bit 0 as 0, or S3/S4/S9/S10 print 'maple busy' and the check fails.

Resumed after the crash. The previous agent had written the RTL, model and testbench. Missing: the planted bugs the mk referenced, tb/bm/dmac and the report. The ddt, irq, extreq and timing groups, plus random programs on non-default seeds, were failing.

RTL fixes:
1. A round-robin pick in the counter-update Bclk now uses the rotated order (hm fig. 14.11).
2. The single-address accepted-cycle FIFO is 4 deep instead of 2, so the BSC bounds the CH2 rate (2 deep capped it at 6 Bcyc or more against the measured 5.77).
3. The class-B junk is latched at commit.
4. The note-16 clear ends a channel-0 DDT edge burst.
5. No commit while rst.man is asserted.
6. A class-B AE is not lost during a module stop.

The model now latches the unit context at commit, like the RTL. The testbench got stub fixes, per-program RNG (--from), RTL-accurate lockstep ordering inside a Bclk, a random quiesce with DME=0 before comparing memory, and new checks: a long edge-DREQ low level, and a manual reset swept over 48 offsets.

SOC.md 6.3 ITLBFILL semantics: emitted only when RF_WR really writes the ITLB entry (never after a TI in the refill window). WI-REF must apply ITLBFILL before an LDTLB record of the same ISN, or the record must carry the copied fields (data[63:6] is free).

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_scif.sv:229 (pop_pend_n = (pop_pend && !tick) || tx_load;) and tb/scif_model.h:314 (same line)
findings.problem: TFRST does not cancel the transmitter's pending pop. The head byte is loaded at S+16, but the FIFO pop happens one tick later, at S+17, through pop_pend, and pop_pend survives TFRST. If the CPU resets the TX FIFO and writes a new byte inside that one-tick window, the stale pop removes the new byte at S+17 and it is never sent. serial.md 3.2.2 step 3 places the pop at S+16, with only its visibility at S+17. The model has the same code, so the co-simulation cannot see the bug. The implementer's random test never reaches this window: with the RTL fix alone (model unfixed), v1-scif still passes.
findings.repro: agents/verify/WI-SER/build/obj/adv corner (X1): SCSMR2 0, SCBRR2 63, SCFCR2 0x0001, SCSCR2 0x0030; SCFTDR2=0xB1; after tick B0+22 and before B0+23: SCFCR2=0x0005, SCFCR2=0x0001, SCFTDR2=0xB2 (SCFDR2.T reads 1); wait 2 frames. The receive FIFO holds only 'b1'; expected 'b1 b2'.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_scif_rx.sv:80 (arm_n = BRK_EN && !rxd && data == 8'd0) and tb/scif_model.h:130; spec serial.md 3.3.5
findings.problem: Break detection only arms after a framing-error frame whose data is 0x00, as serial 3.3.5 says. The manual (hm 16.2.7 BRK) sets BRK after any framing-error frame followed by one frame length of space, and does not store the H'00 that follows. When a break starts inside a frame, the RTL stores an extra 0x00 framing-error byte and sets BRK one frame later. A break that starts at a frame boundary behaves the same under both rules. The spec narrows the manual here; the RTL follows the binding spec.
findings.repro: adv uart U4b: RE, 8N1, brr 0, LOOP=0. RxD2 carries a start bit, D0-D3=1, then space for 35 bit times, then mark, then frame 0x61. RTL: BRK=1, FIFO '0F(FER) 00(FER) 61'. The manual's rule gives '0F(FER) 61'.
findings.fix: The lead decides. Either arm on any framing-error frame (arm_n = BRK_EN && !rxd) in the RTL and the model and correct serial 3.3.5, or keep it and mark it [P] in the spec and the RTL comment.

fix:WI-P4.notes:
No finding was rejected outright. F1, F4, F6 and F7 were confirmed and fixed as proposed, or in an equivalent form.

F2 and F3 were confirmed, but their root cause differs from the verifier's analysis. I used the console once under 9.13, which is this work item's question: no single release chain fits 181, and the older brackets were taken at phases the programs did not control. The phase-resolved probe (tools/hw/p4bus/p4b.c) shows three things:
- A posted write enters the path slot at MA1 like a read, so it can be strobed in MA2 before its MA3 ack.
- The entry is free at strobe + 7 for any size.
- A Pclk bus cycle lasts its transfers + 1 recovery Pcyc.

The verifier's proposed fix kept the MA3 entry load, so it would have left every multi-write row rotated by two phases. The pre-fix RTL was off in 22 of the 31 probe rows; the new RTL matches all 31 at all 4 phases.

F5 and F8 are contract items for the lead: pinned by tests, RTL unchanged.

In the verifier's p4v suite, misc (c) now fails. Its premise is obsolete: it assumed MA3 acceptance, but the CPU write has been in the slot since MA1, so there is no tie. A true same-cycle tie with a posted write is in t_dmac, and the DMAC still wins it.

An intermediate change kept a posted write's pending ack through a master reset. The verifier's randrst caught it (a new request presented during a reset inherited the ack), so I reverted it and added reset case (j) as its regression. The DMAC case it guarded cannot occur: the DMAC starts on bce cycles, so its first strobe opportunity is its ack cycle.

Nothing was committed, and no other work item's files were edited. Scratch and backups are in agents/scratch/WI-P4/; the hardware log is next to its source in tools/hw/p4bus/.

IFILL records carry isn = 0: the IC cannot know the next ISN, so the SoC merger must stamp it (as for board DMAW).

The random test found three model / RTL mismatches from this. v1_ocache now keeps its own requests in program order: a WTB store, a WBB load or an uncached read waits until no older line request is waiting for its accept, and fq is claimed only after f is accepted.
