contract_issues: SOC 3.8 should state that each unit drives xl_req, xl_itlb and xl_va to 0 when it is not requesting. v1_icache used to drive xl_itlb = 1 in every cycle (F4, now fixed).

Accesses killed by a reset (F6). The RTL rule: an access killed after its claim (m + 1 or later: it allocated its buffer or raised its request) is completed. Its fill validates the line, and its stored bytes, WTB store, MOVCA.L allocation and SQ burst stand. An access killed before its claim has no effect. SOC 2.3 names only 'a started write-back / WTB store'; it should adopt this rule, and WI-REF's checker must apply such accesses. v1_ocache has no tap port to report the claim.

TAS.B across a manual reset can deadlock the SoC. A locked read claimed before the reset but not yet accepted stays presented, as SOC 3.3.2 requires. It is taken after the reset and holds the bus for a pair write that the restarted core never issues; the stub keeps its lock across rst.man. SOC 2.3 ('v1_biu queued requests dropped') contradicts 3.3.2. Proposal for WI-BSC: clear the BIU lock at a manual reset.

C1 / C2's m is the tag-compare cycle: MA1, or MA2 when the V-clear comparator holds a same-entry access right behind an OCBI / OCBP / TAS-purge hit. This comparator produces the six OCBI records. v1_ideal_mem (WI-CORE-A) could adopt it so that make v1 matches them too.

Lockstep order for WI-REF (written in the tb/sh4_cache.h header): an OCI / ICI applies after every older acked access, including those whose fills are still in flight (the RTL kills those fills); an IFILL record comes before an ICI in the same cycle; a fetch acked in a CCR write's capture cycle comes before the write.

irsp.busy now means the uncached read is still on the bus: it falls when the word arrives, even if the fetch has not taken it yet. SOC 3.2.1 / 4.1 item 4 should say so. Otherwise a redirect waiting for busy while the fetch is halted (pfz / mah, or an exception's take cycle up to its redirect) would deadlock.
The implementer's contract issues 1-6 in WI-CACHE-impl.md section 6 still stand. Its section 8 item 3 (stld / prefld deferred to M3) is withdrawn: the kern.S loops match on the stub.

TAS.B lock across a manual reset (contract issue): for WI-BSC and the lead.

contract_issues: Sh4CacheIf (SOC.md 6.1) is incomplete for a system model. WI-REF uses sh4sys::CacheX = Sh4CacheIf + ccr_slave, ccr, qacr, ifill, set_lockstep, ic_misses_unfilled, reset, access_rg (with the region), peek, xlat. WI-CACHE's tb/sh4_cache.h provides all of them through a thin adapter. SOC.md should adopt that interface.

MMUCR reads are outside the VOLRD rule, but their LRUI field follows the RTL's speculative fetch hits. Proposal: add MMUCR reads to the VOLRD rule. The model counts the affected reads (n_mmucr_at_reads, in the checker summary). URC itself is exact in the model (mmu 3.6).
WITHDRAWN: the implementer's contract issue 3 (the VOLRD rule misses device reads with OCE=0) was wrong. v1_mmu folds CCR.OCE into dxlat.c, and the model now does the same.
Flash reads (0x00200000-0x0021FFFF) are never VOLRD, so a program that programs the flash cannot run in lockstep (kept from the implementer).

SOC.md 6.3 does not state these record conventions; the checker assumes them and soc_checker.h lists them. (1) Entry register records carry the EXC/IRQ ISN. (2) Reset-type entries are EXC records with EXPEVT 0x020/0x140 and handler A0000000. (3) Two RETIREs of one cycle come in program order. (4) DMAW isn is the next ISN to retire. (5) ITLBFILL addr is the refill VA and LDTLB data is {AA, DA1}. (6) NEW: LDTLB records carry the LDTLB's ISN; v1_mmu leaves isn=0, so WI-SOC must stamp it. (7) NEW: an SQ store whose TLB check fails still writes the queue (mmu R7); its MEMW carries the store's ISN (= the EXC's), although lreq.v is defined as non-faulting. (8) NEW: MEMW data is right-aligned with be used as a byte count; DMAW data is lane-aligned with be = lanes.

Associative-write multiple-hit reset (SOC.md 4.3.2, imprecise). The checker accepts the store retired first or not retired, and rejects any younger retirement before the EXC 0x140. SOC.md should fix the RTL's shape, and say whether a paired follower may retire first.

Channel-B data break (SOC.md 4.3.2/4.3.5). Exactly one follower RETIRE is accepted. [P] If the follower raises its own completion entry (TRAPA, a break), the older data break wins with SPC after the follower. [P] If the follower is a delayed branch, SPC is its slot. WI-CORE-A should confirm both, or SOC.md should fix them.

ITLB multiple hit vs a UBC pre-execution break on the same instruction: the ISS now follows hm Table 5.2 (the 0x140 reset, level 1, wins) [M]. SOC.md 4.3.2 should say so for WI-CORE-A's D-stage priority; 9.9 cannot measure it.

Fetch-ahead vs fill records (SOC.md 6.2). IFILL/ITLBFILL records can replace the line or entry of an instruction already fetched but not yet retired. [P] The model serves such fetches from the last 16 replaced lines/entries, and for 16 instructions after an ICI or IC array write from the invalidated entry. Only an unexplained miss is flagged. SOC.md 6.2 should state the IC-fill and ITLB-refill injection rule with this in mind.

Asynchronous resets (WDT, H-UDI, the RESET pin) have no lockstep injection rule in SOC.md 6.2, so the checker cannot follow them. WI-CACHE's new note in tb/sh4_cache.h (a reset completes an access killed after its claim) also needs a lockstep rule.

core-integration 8.2 says URC depends on speculative fetch-side refills; mmu 3.6 [HW D1] and v1_mmu say refills never change URC. The model keeps the core-integration exemption, which is conservative. The spec text should be reconciled.
Kept from the implementer, unchanged: p4[] indexed by port plus additive Sh4Board members; WI-EXC expected.json relaxations; the D-stage FD-first priority for undecoded H'Fxxx codes.

When a two-access instruction's second access faults, does the first access's ma_commit count URC in the RTL? The model counts nothing for a faulting instruction. This shows only in an LDTLB index or a MMUCR read.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_core.sv, lreq always_comb (lreq.v, around line 1335)
findings.problem: A UBC post-execution break on lane 0 is a completion-type MA take. It kills everything younger (SOC.md 4.3.2, kill > K), including the paired lane-1 follower that reached MA in the same cycle. lreq.v does not look at the lane-0 take, so the killed follower's access is still presented and performed. A store writes memory, an OCBI / PREF / OCBWB acts on the cache, and ma_commit (URC) pulses. A slow follower also delays the take through mah. This is an imprecise exception: the ISS never executes the store.
findings.repro: From the repo root: make -C agents/verify/WI-CORE-A build; agents/verify/WI-CORE-A/obj/vx/tb --only vx_ubc_post_l1acc_add_st. The program is ubc_prog(BARA = x, PCBA = 1); x: ADD #1,R5 ; MOV.L R6,@R8 (paired). Result: [8C020080] DEADBEEF (ISS A5808080), entry 1E0 with SPC = the store. The same holds for the variants _mov_stb, _cmp_fmovs, _bt_nt_st, _add_stpre and _slow (6 FAILs). The control, with the store one group later, passes.
findings.fix: Gate lane 1's request with the lane-0 take: lreq.v = ... && !kill_ma && !(l == 1 && ma_tk[0]). An alternative is to latch a no-access bit at EX from the existing ex_stop1 condition. The fix was validated in agents/scratch/WI-CORE-A-verify/fix/v1_core.sv: the 6 F1 tests pass; the repo directed tests 561/561; repo fuzz and fuzz-irq 3000/3000 each; vxfuzz 6000/6000 and vxfuzz-irq 4000/4000; soc-design c1-c2c, c1i and ci3 check.py PASS. findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_core.sv, ex_f (the FPU's EX view, around line 1706), together with v1_fpu's mq write-back
findings.problem: A faulting LDS.L @Rm+,MACL or MACH (misaligned, user-mode P1 or TLB miss) sets MACL or MACH to 0. v1_fpu inserts the multiplier 'def' record from the core's EX latch in the cycle the fault is found. The take happens one cycle later, at MA, and the core gates ex_f only with kex. v1_fpu writes MACH / MACL when eta runs out, whether or not the operand arrived, and the killed MA micro-op never delivers it. A re-execution-type fault must leave MACH / MACL unchanged (exceptions-intc 3.3). This case is not in the repo's XFAIL list. The repo's mac_* tests pass only because an unloaded MAC operand is 0.
findings.repro: obj/vx/tb --only vx_macfault_ldsl_macl_dae (LDS.L @R9+,MACL with R9 = BUF + 2): MACL 00000000 (ISS 55550000). vx_macfault_ldsl_mach_dae gives MACH 00000000 (ISS 44440000). The _user and _tlb variants fail the same way.
findings.fix: Core side: ex_f[l] = (kex[l] || (ex[l].v && ex_fin[l].uk == UK_NORM && ex_fin[l].fx != FX_NONE)) ? '0 : ex[l]. This was validated in the same scratch core, and all repo gates still pass. The alternative is for WI-CORE-F's ISN kill to reach the mq records; they carry no ISN today.

findings.where: rtl/v1/v1_core.sv, S-stage take (stake: tk_spc = sl[s_yl].ftea), and the SOC.md 4.3.5 / debug-ubc-hudi 4.3 [P] data-break SPC rule
findings.problem: A channel-B data break (DBEB) whose access pairs with a one-cycle delayed branch (BRA, BSR, BT/S, BF/S) sets SPC = 'the first instruction issued after the group', which is the branch's slot. The entry therefore lands between the branch and its slot. On return the slot runs as an ordinary instruction and execution falls through, so the taken branch is lost. For BSR, PR is written but the subroutine never runs. Every other break kind defers to after the slot, and exceptions-intc 3.5 treats a branch and its slot as one unit. This case was not measured on the console.
findings.repro: obj/vx/tb --only vx_ubc_data_pair_bra (also _bsr, _bts). The program is SETT ; NOP ; x: MOV.L @R9,R1 ; BRA t (paired) ; slot ADD #1,R6 ; fall-through ADD #1,R3 ... t: ADD #1,R4, with the logging handler resuming at SPC. Result: R3 00001334 (the fall-through executed), R4 00001444 (the target not executed), R6 00001667.
findings.fix: When the S group's youngest instruction is a one-cycle delayed branch whose slot is not in the group, either let the slot complete and take with SPC = the branch continuation (dly_cont), as the post-execution break does, or set SPC = the branch. SOC.md 4.3.5 / 9.16 should state which.

findings.where: v1_core sleep_req (a level) against v1_cpg / CpgStub (rising edge); SOC.md 2.5
findings.problem: After a wake whose request is gone when run returns, the core stays in the sleep state with run = 1 and sleep_req held high. The CPG only acts on a new rising edge, so the CPU never powers down again until the next interrupt, and PMCTR counts meanwhile. SOC.md 2.5 draws the FSM as level-sensitive.
findings.repro: obj/vx/tb --only vx_sleep_spurious_wake -v (marked XFAIL as an open item). A 3-cycle pulse with RESYNC 7 gives the CPG one sleep and 301 run = 0 cycles, then about 1,200 cycles awake while asleep.
findings.fix: Either the core drops sleep_req for one cycle when run rises, or v1_cpg re-arms sleep_q when it leaves RESYNC. Record the decision in SOC.md 2.5 / 4.4.3.

contract_issues: SOC.md 3.2.2 rule 1: lreq.v must also be 0 for the lane-1 follower when the lane-0 micro-op takes at MA in the same cycle. The rule should also list the SQ store with a TLB fault, which is presented although it faults [HW mmu 3.8].
SOC.md 3.2.2 rule 4: kill_ma does not fire for a data break whose access group ends in a one-cycle delayed branch, because the slot's access completes.

SOC.md 4.3.2 / 4.3.5 / 9.16 and debug-ubc-hudi 4.3 [HW c1k]: when the access group ends in BRA / BSR / BT/S / BF/S, the slot completes, the data break is taken at the slot's MA commit point (completion type), and SPC = the branch's continuation (target, or slot + 2 when not taken). The case where the slot faults is [P]: SPC = the branch.

WI-REF, tb/sh4_iss.h: step_past_data_break must also run the slot of a delayed-branch follower and re-arm SPC = the continuation. The plain step() path enters before the branch, which the console refutes, so v1-exc checks these rows against explicit expectations instead of the ISS.

SOC.md 2.5 / 4.4.3: sleep_req is a level that the core drops while run = 0 and in the first cycle after run rises, so a CPG may take either its level or its rising edge. v1_cpg's header comment about a held level describes the old core.
SOC.md 4.3.1: 'no timing decision reads the ISN' is true again, because the claim now picks younger micro-ops by pipeline position.
SOC.md 4.3.3 / 4.3.4 item 2 / 9.1: the branch stop applies to issued micro-ops as well as queued ones, and a claimant is an instruction, counted at its first micro-op [P].
WI-CORE-F: v1_fpu's multiplier records need the ISN kill. After that, the core's interim exf_mul hiding and its fhzc hazard can be removed.
WI-CORE-B: q0_fx / q1_fx (with vec400) replace the core's interim q_fx / fpois / slot0_rte, and must also suppress the ireq. Poison flags for q2 and q3 are needed for the claim's pre-decode.
